Thanks again for taking the call today, Samir — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side:

- ACME will evaluate serving-sensitive routing: low-latency region routing for user-facing chat, and cost-optimized batch routing for bulk document embeddings.
- Key integration points: SDK auth (API keys + optional mTLS), structured output/tool-calling for your triage flows, and embeddings + reranker for search relevance.
- Policy needs: latency SLOs for chat (p95 < 200ms), fallback chains to cheaper models under capacity pressure, and region-aware data residency.

Action items (proposed owner / timeline):
1) Share SDK quickstart + auth examples (we attached a short quickstart) — owner: Marissa (today)
2) Draft model routing policy examples showing latency vs cost tradeoffs — owner: Dev (EOD Fri)

4) Follow-up call to review policy YAML and SDK walk-through — propose Tue 3/16 10am PT (Samir/ Priya)

- Do you plan to host any inference traffic in eu-west (EU) for GDPR-sensitive customers?
- Any mandatory handshake or PKI constraints for auth (e.g., must use customer-managed KMS or mTLS)?

Attaching: redwood-sdk-quickstart.md (SDK snippets + auth), preliminary model-routing-policy-draft.yaml

Thanks — I’ll wait for your availability for the follow-up.

Hey Samir / Marissa — following up with the policy examples I promised. Notes below and attached YAML.

1) Auth: Redwood supports API key + optional customer-managed KMS for enveloping secrets. For private deployment we also support mutual TLS (mTLS) termination on the VPC ingress; config example in quickstart. If you need HSM integration, we have a support path (we've done AWS CloudHSM & Azure Key Vault HSM).

2) Model routing patterns (examples):
- Latency-first route (chat): route requests from us-west + eu-west to low-latency model variants (quantized LLM on GPUs) with p95 SLO target. Fallback chain: primary low-latency model -> smaller/cheaper variant -> queued/batched offline if throughput constrained.
- Cost-first route (bulk embeddings): batch in bulk windows (5–15s), route to quantized CPU/GPU embeddings runners; fallback to cheaper quantized CPU runners if GPU pool full.
- Region-aware routing: policy field region_preference that pins requests to same-region runners; if capacity constrained, policy can opt into cross-region routing with encryption-in-transit and data residency audit logs enabled.

3) Structured output & tool-calling: include schema for tool responses to keep outputs deterministic (we recommend JSONSchema + function/tool-call envelope; example in SDK snippet). This helps reranker to score responses deterministically.

4) Reranker latency guidance: for real-time reranker at 1M doc index we suggest a two-stage approach: candidate retrieval via approximate nearest neighbors (50–200ms depending on index), then a lightweight reranker model tuned for sub-100ms inference p99 on our dedicated fleet. If you need p95 < 100ms, we should plan dedicated capacity for the reranker.

Please find attached: model-routing-policy-draft.yaml (policy examples), and a short explainer on embedding batch configs.

Proposed next technical agenda for Tue:
- Walk through policy YAML and map to ACME routing requirements (15m)
- SDK auth + sample code run (20m)
- Reranker sizing and dedicated capacity options (10m)
- Open Qs / Triage (15m)
